name: GHRP-5

angle.text: GHRP-5, called the Momany peptide, is grouped with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as a GH-releasing peptide that bodybuilders consider for muscle and leanness. Evidence is laboratory and anti-doping literature, with no human trials.

summary: The "Momany peptide": a GH-releasing peptide with lab and anti-doping papers but no human trials.
note: Prohibited in competitive sport; no human clinical studies found.
currentQuick:
GHRP-5 is a synthetic peptide in the growth hormone-releasing peptide family, also called the Momany peptide, and is discussed in muscle-building contexts.
The literature is limited to anti-doping chemistry and a few laboratory studies. No human clinical studies were found.
How it works: It is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor, and one laboratory study reported it also releases prolactin.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data were found. It is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.
deepLead:
GHRP-5 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide, also referred to in the literature as the Momany peptide. Analytical papers group it with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as synthetic met-enkephalin analogues with unnatural D-amino acids designed to stimulate growth hormone release.
Published work on GHRP-5 is sparse: anti-doping chemistry, peptide-handling studies, and a laboratory study of its prolactin-releasing activity. No human clinical studies were found.

name: Livoletide

angle.text: Livoletide is an investigational appetite peptide built for hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome. Fat-loss interest comes from its status as an experimental appetite and body-weight drug; its pivotal trial was terminated, and no cosmetic use has been studied.

summary: An investigational unacylated-ghrelin peptide built for Prader-Willi hunger, with its pivotal trial terminated.
note: Never approved; no studies in people seeking cosmetic fat loss.
currentQuick:
Livoletide is an experimental peptide designed to curb the extreme hunger of Prader-Willi syndrome. It mimics unacylated ghrelin, a form of the hunger hormone that does not activate the usual ghrelin receptor.
Its main phase 2b/3 trial was terminated, and no study has tested it for appearance-related fat loss.
How it works: It replaces a reported relative deficit of unacylated ghrelin in people with PWS, with the hypothesis that this reduces hyperphagia.
Risks and caveats: It is investigational and unapproved. Safety information in the sources is limited to nonclinical and juvenile toxicity work and trial records.
deepLead:
Livoletide (AZP-531) is a cyclic peptide analogue of unacylated ghrelin that was developed to treat hyperphagia, the intense and persistent hunger, in Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS). Its appearance-related interest stems from its status as an experimental appetite and body-weight drug.
Its pivotal phase 2b/3 trial, ZEPHYR, enrolled 158 participants and is recorded on ClinicalTrials.gov as terminated. It has not been approved, and no study has tested it for cosmetic fat loss in people without PWS.

name: Lenomorelin (Ghrelin)

angle.text: Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that raises hunger and stimulates growth hormone, so fat-loss and muscle communities discuss it as a lever on appetite and body composition. It is central to appetite science; use for appearance is untested.

summary: The stomach hunger hormone and GH secretagogue; central to appetite science, untested for looks.
note: Studied in cachexia and other clinical settings, not for cosmetic use.
currentQuick:
Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that signals hunger and also prompts growth hormone release. Its INN is lenomorelin.
It matters to body-composition discussion because appetite and growth hormone both affect fat and muscle, but no study has tested it for appearance goals.
How it works: Once an octanoyl group is attached by the enzyme GOAT, ghrelin activates the GHS-R1a receptor in the brain, pituitary and gut, driving hunger and growth hormone release.
Risks and caveats: Clinical use has been investigational, in conditions such as cancer cachexia. The sources reviewed give no safety summary, and it is not an approved appearance treatment.
deepLead:
Ghrelin, whose international nonproprietary name is lenomorelin, is a peptide hormone made mainly by enteroendocrine cells of the stomach. It is widely called the "hunger hormone" because it raises the drive to eat, and it also stimulates growth hormone release from the pituitary, which gave it its name.
It is identified in 1999 as the ligand of the growth hormone secretagogue receptor. Its relevance to looksmaxxing lies in body composition: appetite, fat mass and growth hormone. Administered ghrelin has been studied in clinical settings such as cancer cachexia and frailty, not as a cosmetic agent.

name: Cortistatin-14

angle.text: Cortistatin-14 is a brain neuropeptide related to somatostatin that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, which draws occasional recovery and GH-axis speculation. It has been studied as basic science only, with nothing on appearance.

summary: A somatostatin-related brain peptide that also binds ghrelin-type receptors; basic science only, nothing on looks.
note: No human data for any appearance use.
currentQuick:
Cortistatin-14 is a short neuropeptide closely related to somatostatin, first noted for its activity in the cortex. It has been studied in receptor pharmacology and neuroscience.
No published trial has tested it for appearance, muscle or recovery, and it is not an approved drug.
How it works: It binds all five somatostatin receptors, has been reported to bind GHS (ghrelin-type) receptors in human pituitary, and activates the itch receptor MRGPRX2.
Risks and caveats: Human safety data are essentially limited to small endocrine studies. It has no approved product or regulatory status as a medicine.
deepLead:
Cortistatin-14 is a naturally occurring neuropeptide related to somatostatin. It was named for its predominantly cortical expression and its ability to depress cortical activity, and it shares 11 of its 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14 even though the two peptides are encoded by separate genes .
Unlike somatostatin, cortistatin has been reported to bind growth hormone secretagogue (GHS) receptors in human pituitary tissue, and it binds all five cloned somatostatin receptors . More recently, structural work identified it as an endogenous agonist of the itch-related receptor MRGPRX2 . It is a research peptide and has no approved medical use.
No published human study has tested cortistatin-14 for any appearance-related purpose. The literature consists of basic neuroscience, receptor pharmacology and a small number of human endocrine studies.

name: LUM-201

angle.text: LUM-201 is ibutamoren (MK-0677), an oral GH secretagogue that physique users discuss as a pill-form route to higher GH and IGF-1 for muscle and leanness. It is in trials for children with GH deficiency; looks outcomes are untested.

summary: An oral GH-secretagogue (ibutamoren) in trials for children with GH deficiency; nothing tests it for looks.
note: Investigational; evidence is in children with diagnosed GHD only.
currentQuick:
LUM-201 is the development name for ibutamoren (MK-0677), a daily oral drug that stimulates the body's own growth hormone release. It is being tested as an alternative to injections in children with growth hormone deficiency.
Phase 2 trials reported growth responses in some children, and a Phase 3 trial is under way. No study has examined it for appearance in healthy people.
How it works: It activates the GH secretagogue (ghrelin-type) receptor, prompting pulsatile GH release, which in turn raises IGF-1.
Risks and caveats: It is investigational and not approved. Safety data come from pediatric trials, with long-term safety extensions registered.
deepLead:
LUM-201 (ibutamoren, formerly MK-0677) is an orally administered growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist under clinical development for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (PGHD) . It is developed as a daily oral alternative to injected growth hormone.
Phase 2 trials in children with idiopathic PGHD have examined growth responses, and researchers have proposed a pretreatment test to identify children with enough residual hypothalamic-pituitary function to respond . A Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial is registered and recruiting . It is not approved by any regulator.
No published study has tested LUM-201 for appearance outcomes in healthy people.

name: IGF-1 DES

angle.text: Forum users inject IGF-1 DES locally in hopes of growing the jaw, chin and neck, and stack it with other agents for facial remodelling. Evidence is cell and animal data on protein synthesis; the facial-growth idea is anecdotal.

summary: A truncated IGF-1 analogue forum users inject locally for jaw and muscle growth; only cell and animal data exist.
note: No human studies; IGF signalling is linked to growth of prostate and other tissues in animal work.
currentQuick:
IGF-1 DES is a shortened version of IGF-1 that binds less to carrier proteins and was more potent than IGF-1 in rat muscle cell assays. Forum users discuss injecting it into the chin, jaw or neck to build tissue.
No human study has tested it for appearance; the research is in cells and animals.
How it works: It activates IGF-1 signalling with reduced interference from IGF binding proteins, which in lab studies increases its effect on protein synthesis and cell growth.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data exist. Animal work reported prostate overgrowth with IGF-1(des) expression, and IGF signalling is described as a cancer-risk factor when elevated. It has no approved human use.
deepLead:
IGF-1 DES, written des(1-3)IGF-1, is a truncated form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) lacking the first three amino acids at the N-terminus. The truncation lowers its affinity for IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), and in laboratory assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells .
It is a research peptide, not an approved medicine. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, users discuss injecting it locally, for example into the chin, jaw or neck, with the aim of growing muscle or reshaping features . Believers cite its potency; researchers note that the supporting work is in cell cultures and animals.
No published human study has tested IGF-1 DES for muscle or facial appearance. Published work is limited to in vitro and animal studies.

name: Somatrogon

angle.text: Somatrogon is a weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency, so it comes up in height discussions. It has been studied in children with deficiency; data for added height without deficiency do not exist.

summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency; no evidence for height gain without a deficiency.
note: Prescription drug for diagnosed GHD; trials are in children with deficiency only.
currentQuick:
Somatrogon (Ngenla) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved in the US for children aged 3 and older whose bodies do not make enough growth hormone. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin.
Trials involve children with a diagnosed deficiency. No study has tested it for height in children without one.
How it works: It binds the growth hormone receptor, activates STAT5b signalling and raises IGF-1, promoting linear growth.
Risks and caveats: The label lists warnings such as neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Somatrogon (MOD-4023; brand name Ngenla) is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analogue given by subcutaneous injection once a week. In the United States it is indicated for children aged 3 years and older with growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone .
In phase 3 trials, weekly somatrogon was compared with daily somatropin in prepubertal children with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), including a 12-month open-label randomised study and a study in Japanese children . Reviews of the three long-acting growth hormones (lonapegsomatropin, somatrogon and somapacitan) describe non-inferior height velocity and similar safety profiles to daily growth hormone in 52-week trials .
It is a prescription medicine for diagnosed deficiency. No study has tested it for height gain in children without a diagnosed deficiency.

name: Lonapegsomatropin

angle.text: Lonapegsomatropin is a weekly prescription GH prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed deficiency, and is mentioned in height-focused circles. Trials involve people with GH deficiency; data on height in people without it are absent.

summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed GH deficiency; no data for height without deficiency.
note: Prescription drug for diagnosed GHD.
currentQuick:
Lonapegsomatropin (Skytrofa) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved by the FDA in 2021 for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin.
Trials involve people with a diagnosed deficiency, and none tests it for height in people without one.
How it works: It is a pegylated growth hormone prodrug that releases somatropin, which binds the GH receptor and acts partly through IGF-1.
Risks and caveats: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Lonapegsomatropin (brand name Skytrofa; development name TransCon hGH) is a once-weekly, long-acting prodrug of growth hormone given by subcutaneous injection. The US FDA approved it in August 2021 for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (GHD) .
The US label covers children aged 1 year and older weighing at least 11.5 kg with growth failure due to inadequate endogenous GH secretion, and adults with GHD . Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin in treatment-naive and switched children .
It is a prescription medicine for diagnosed deficiency. No trial has tested it for height or appearance in people without a deficiency.

name: Somapacitan

angle.text: Somapacitan is a weekly prescription growth hormone approved for GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions, so height-focused users watch it. Studies cover those diagnosed groups; data on height outside them are absent.

summary: A weekly albumin-binding growth hormone for diagnosed GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions; no data for height otherwise.
note: Prescription drug; trials in diagnosed conditions only.
currentQuick:
Somapacitan (Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection. In the US it is labelled for growth hormone deficiency in children and adults and for several pediatric short-stature conditions.
Trials compared it with daily growth hormone in diagnosed patients. No study has tested it for height or appearance in people without a diagnosis.
How it works: It is a growth hormone derivative that binds albumin reversibly, extending its action, and binds the GH receptor with effects partly mediated by IGF-1.
Risks and caveats: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Somapacitan (brand name Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone derivative that binds reversibly to albumin, given by subcutaneous injection . The US label covers pediatric patients aged 2.5 years and older with growth hormone deficiency (GHD), short stature born small for gestational age, Noonan syndrome growth failure and idiopathic short stature, as well as adults with GHD .
Phase 3 trials examined it in adults (REAL 1) and children (REAL 4), with long-term follow-up of the phase 2 REAL 3 study reaching four years . Reviews describe non-inferior height velocity and a similar safety profile compared with daily growth hormone for the long-acting class .
It is a prescription medicine. One looksmax.org thread asks whether it is worth using, with no substantive discussion found.

name: Mecasermin

angle.text: Mecasermin is prescription recombinant IGF-1 for children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, and it is talked about in height forums as a growth lever. It has been studied in that narrow group; use for height beyond it is untested.

summary: Prescription recombinant IGF-1 for rare severe IGF-1 deficiency in children; talked about for height but only studied in that narrow group.
note: Approved only for children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency; label warns of hypoglycemia and other serious effects.
currentQuick:
Mecasermin (Increlex) is lab-made IGF-1 given by injection. It is approved in the US for children 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, or GH gene deletion with antibodies to GH.
It comes up in height discussions because IGF-1 mediates growth. Published trials involve children with the rare deficiency, not people of normal growth.
How it works: It replaces the IGF-1 that GH would normally trigger, acting on the type 1 IGF receptor to drive growth and also lowering blood glucose in an insulin-like way.
Risks and caveats: The label lists hypoglycemia (including seizures), allergic reactions, intracranial hypertension, enlarged tonsils, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, scoliosis progression and malignancy as risks. It is prescription-only and not indicated after growth plates close.
deepLead:
Mecasermin, sold as Increlex, is a recombinant form of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) made in E. coli and given by subcutaneous injection.  The US label indicates it for growth failure in children aged 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, or with growth hormone (GH) gene deletion who have developed neutralizing antibodies to GH. 
The label states that it is not a substitute for GH in GH's approved indications.  Its relevance to appearance communities is height: it is sometimes raised in discussions of increasing stature. Published trials and registries concern children with a defined, rare deficiency and are not studies of height gain in people with normal IGF-1. 
Documented adverse effects in the label include hypoglycemia, hypersensitivity reactions, intracranial hypertension, tonsil and adenoid enlargement, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, scoliosis progression and malignant neoplasia.

name: Pegvisomant

chain: Less GH-driven bone and soft-tissue growth
angle.text: Pegvisomant is discussed in appearance circles as the opposite of a growth hormone booster: it lowers IGF-1 and is used in acromegaly, where excess GH enlarges the jaw, brow and hands. Its cosmetic relevance is as a reference point for GH-driven facial change; it has not been studied for cosmetic use.

summary: Prescription GH-receptor blocker for acromegaly; its appearance relevance is as the opposite of a GH booster, and it has no cosmetic studies.
note: Approved only for acromegaly; label warns of liver toxicity and hypoglycemia in diabetes.
currentQuick:
Pegvisomant (Somavert) is an injectable drug that blocks the growth hormone receptor. It is approved for acromegaly, a condition of GH excess causing enlarged hands, feet and facial features.
It appears in appearance discussions as a GH-axis compound. No published study tests it for cosmetic use.
How it works: It binds the GH receptor and prevents GH from signaling, which lowers IGF-1.
Risks and caveats: The label lists liver enzyme elevations, hypoglycemia in diabetic patients, injection-site lipohypertrophy and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Pegvisomant, sold as Somavert, is a pegylated growth hormone (GH) analog that blocks the GH receptor.  It is approved in the US for acromegaly in patients who responded inadequately to surgery or radiation, or for whom those are unsuitable, with the treatment goal of normalizing IGF-1. 
Acromegaly produces enlargement of the hands, feet and facial features, which is why the drug is sometimes mentioned in appearance and height forums as a GH-axis compound. No published trial in the supplied literature tests it for cosmetic purposes in people without GH excess. 
Documented risks in the label include hypoglycemia in patients with diabetes, liver toxicity, lipohypertrophy and systemic hypersensitivity.

name: Bivamelagon

angle.text: Bivamelagon is an oral MC4R agonist that fat-loss followers watch as a possible appetite-control route to a leaner look. It is being studied for weight gain after hypothalamic damage; no data exist in cosmetic or general fat-loss use.

summary: Investigational oral MC4R agonist tested for hypothalamic obesity; no data in cosmetic use.
note: Not approved; studied only in a rare medical obesity.
currentQuick:
Bivamelagon is an experimental once-daily oral drug that activates the MC4R, a brain receptor involved in appetite and weight regulation.
It has been tested in a phase 2 trial in people with hypothalamic obesity. It is not approved.
How it works: It stimulates MC4R signaling in the brain's weight-regulating pathway.
Risks and caveats: Not approved anywhere; safety data are limited to early trials in a small patient group.
deepLead:
Bivamelagon (also LB54640) is an investigational oral melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) agonist.  It is being studied in hypothalamic obesity, weight gain following damage to the hypothalamus, and is not an approved drug.
A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in acquired hypothalamic obesity was reported in the Journal of the Endocrine Society in 2025.  A registered phase 2 study (n=28) finished, and a long-term extension study (n=25) began enrolling by invitation in November 2025.

name: RM-718

angle.text: RM-718 is a weekly MC4R agonist followed by fat-loss researchers as a possible route to appetite control and a leaner physique. It is in early trials for rare obesity syndromes, and no results or cosmetic data are available.

summary: Experimental weekly MC4R agonist in early trials for rare obesity syndromes; no results or cosmetic data.
note: Investigational only; the only available source is a trial listing.
currentQuick:
RM-718 is an experimental drug from Rhythm that activates the MC4R pathway of appetite regulation, designed for weekly dosing.
It is in an early phase 1/2 study in healthy volunteers and people with hypothalamic obesity or Prader-Willi syndrome.
How it works: It is an MC4R agonist.
Risks and caveats: Not approved; no published safety results were located.
deepLead:
RM-718 is an investigational melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) agonist developed by Rhythm, described as a weekly-dosed compound.  A phase 1/2 study of RM-718 in healthy subjects and in patients with MC4R pathway impairment, including hypothalamic obesity and Prader-Willi syndrome, began in March 2024 with 111 participants. 
It is not approved. No published results were located, and the only source is the trial registration.

name: PL-8177

angle.text: PL-8177 is an MC1r agonist that tanning-peptide readers connect to melanocortin-driven pigmentation and a deeper tan. It has been studied in inflammatory bowel and eye models rather than for tanning, so the appearance link is untested.

summary: Experimental oral MC1r peptide in trials for ulcerative colitis; not studied for tanning or appearance.
note: Investigational; its studied purpose is inflammation, not pigment.
currentQuick:
PL-8177 is an experimental oral peptide that activates the melanocortin 1 receptor, the same receptor family linked to skin pigmentation.
Its published and registered research concerns inflammation, including a small ulcerative colitis trial.
How it works: It mimics alpha-MSH at MC1r, which in animal models reduced intestinal and ocular inflammation.
Risks and caveats: Not approved; human safety data are limited to early-phase trials.
deepLead:
PL-8177 is an investigational oral peptide agonist of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1r).  It has been studied for inflammatory conditions, not for tanning or pigmentation: preclinical work with PL-8177 and PL-8331 examined prevention and reversal of intestinal and ocular inflammation in animal models. 
A phase 2a trial in active ulcerative colitis (n=16) began in September 2022.  No studies were found of PL-8177 for skin pigmentation or appearance.

name: SHU-9119

chain: Alters appetite signalling in lab models
angle.text: SHU-9119 is a melanocortin antagonist used in rodent studies as a tool to block appetite-regulating signalling, which is how it enters fat-loss discussions. It has no human studies, and its appearance relevance is as a research reference for melanocortin agonists.

summary: Lab melanocortin antagonist used in rodent appetite research; no human studies and no approved use.
note: Research-only peptide studied in animals.
currentQuick:
SHU-9119 is a research peptide that blocks melanocortin receptors. Scientists have used it in rats to study appetite, body weight and insulin action.
It has no approved use and no human trials were found.
How it works: It antagonizes melanocortin receptors (MC3R and MC4R) in the brain, opposing the signal of alpha-MSH.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data exist; in animals, blocking this pathway increased feeding.
deepLead:
SHU-9119 (also written SHU9119) is a laboratory melanocortin receptor antagonist used in animal research on appetite and energy balance.  Studies in rats infused it into the brain's third ventricle as a tool to block melanocortin signaling, alongside the agonist alpha-MSH. 
It is not a drug approved for humans, and no human clinical studies were found. It is a research peptide whose effects in animals include increased feeding and altered insulin action.

name: S-23

angle.text: S-23 is a SARM sold as a research chemical, and users take it hoping for muscle gain with fewer steroid-like effects, building a more muscular physique. It was developed as a male contraceptive candidate; its muscle effects are based on animal work and anecdote, with no published human trials.

summary: An investigational nonsteroidal SARM developed as a male contraceptive candidate; no human trials are published and it appears as a gray-market research chemical.
note: Investigational only; no published human studies; sold as a designer drug.
currentQuick:
S-23 is an experimental selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by GTx, Inc. as a possible male hormonal contraceptive. It binds the androgen receptor more tightly than the older SARM andarine.
Its appearance relevance comes from the broader SARM category, which is used in muscle-building circles. No human trials of S-23 are described in the sources consulted.
How it works: It is a nonsteroidal compound that binds the androgen receptor (reported Ki of about 1.7 nM). In animal work it was reported to suppress spermatogenesis in a dose-dependent way, with recovery after treatment stopped.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data are described. SARMs as a class are banned by WADA, and compounds sold online as research chemicals have been reported to be mislabeled. Class-level reports include liver enzyme elevation and suppression of the body's own testosterone production.
deepLead:
S-23 (also called Mastorin) is an investigational selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by GTx, Inc. as a candidate male hormonal contraceptive. It is a nonsteroidal compound that binds the androgen receptor with higher affinity than the older SARM andarine.
Animal studies reported in the literature summarised on Wikipedia describe a favourable ratio of anabolic to androgenic effects and dose-dependent suppression of sperm production that recovered after treatment ended. The sources consulted describe no published human trials. It was reported as a novel designer drug by 2020.

name: S-40503

chain: Anabolic effect on muscle and bone
angle.text: S-40503 is a SARM noted in muscle-building circles for its tissue-selective androgen receptor activity, which is linked to lean mass gain. It was studied in rat osteoporosis models and is known mostly from doping-control research; there are no human efficacy data.

summary: A preclinical nonsteroidal SARM tested in rat osteoporosis models; known mainly from doping-control research, with no human efficacy data.
note: Preclinical only; detectable in doping tests.
currentQuick:
S-40503 is an experimental nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). It was described in 2003 in rat models of osteoporosis, where it showed bone-building activity.
No human clinical trials are listed in the sources consulted. It is discussed mainly in anti-doping analytical literature.
How it works: It binds the androgen receptor with nanomolar affinity and preferentially over other nuclear receptors. In orchiectomized rats given it for 4 weeks, researchers evaluated its bone effects against dihydrotestosterone.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data are described. SARMs are prohibited by WADA, and doping-control laboratories have developed methods to detect S-40503 in human plasma.
deepLead:
S-40503 is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) first described in 2003 as a compound developed to pursue tissue-selective androgen receptor activity. It bound the androgen receptor with nanomolar affinity, with preference for it among nuclear receptors, and was evaluated in rat models of osteoporosis against dihydrotestosterone.
Later literature on it comes mostly from doping control, where laboratories described identifying it in human plasma as an emerging drug with potential for misuse. The sources consulted describe no human trials.

name: LGD-2226

chain: Anabolic effect on muscle and bone
angle.text: LGD-2226 is a SARM that users take hoping to add muscle with less prostate stimulation than testosterone. Animal studies showed anabolic effects on muscle and bone; there are no human trials, and it is sold as a research chemical.

summary: An experimental quinolinone SARM studied in animals for muscle and bone; no human trials and sold only as a research chemical.
note: Unapproved investigational drug; banned in sport; no human safety data.
currentQuick:
LGD-2226 is an experimental drug of the SARM class that was reported in 2006 and tested in animals for muscle and bone effects.
No human trials were found. Its place in looksmaxxing is limited to physique-focused circles where SARMs are sold online as research chemicals.
How it works: It binds and activates the androgen receptor, with animal data indicating larger effects on muscle and bone than on the prostate compared with testosterone.
Risks and caveats: No human safety data exist for this compound. SARMs as a class have been linked to liver enzyme elevations and hormone suppression, and they are banned in sport and unapproved by the FDA.
deepLead:
LGD-2226 is an investigational, orally active, nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the quinolinone chemical class, reported in the medicinal chemistry literature in 2006 . It was characterised in animal studies as an androgen receptor agonist with anabolic effects on muscle and bone and comparatively smaller effects on prostate weight and luteinizing hormone than testosterone .
It has been researched for muscle wasting and osteoporosis rather than for cosmetic purposes . It is not an approved medicine, SARMs as a class are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency, and no published human trial of LGD-2226 was identified . Its relevance to appearance culture is limited to its use in the muscle-building (physique) segment, where SARMs are sold online as research chemicals .

name: LGD-2941

angle.text: LGD-2941 is a quinolinone SARM that muscle-building communities treat as a lean mass candidate. It was investigated for cachexia and hypogonadism, then discontinued after Phase I, so its appearance use rests on almost no public data.

summary: A discontinued quinolinone SARM with almost no public data and no human results.
note: Development ended; effectively no human data.
currentQuick:
LGD-2941 is an experimental SARM that was explored for muscle wasting, low testosterone and bone loss.
Its development has reportedly stopped and there are no published human results.
How it works: Like other SARMs, it is designed to activate the androgen receptor selectively in muscle and bone.
Risks and caveats: No safety data are public. It is unapproved, and SARMs generally are banned in sport.
deepLead:
LGD-2941 (also LGD-122941) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the quinolinone class that was investigated for cachexia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis . Wikipedia reports that it is no longer being developed, and its Phase I trial was discontinued .
Very little published information exists beyond its chemistry; a 2008 paper on related oxazinoquinolinone SARMs is the main cited literature . It is not about appearance enhancement per se, and no community material or human results were identified.

name: LGD-3303

chain: Anabolic effect in muscle and bone
angle.text: LGD-3303 is an oral SARM discussed by people seeking muscle gain through selective androgen receptor activity. Published work covers only animal and in vitro studies in rats and horses; human muscle effects are untested.

summary: A Ligand Pharmaceuticals nonsteroidal SARM tested only in rats and horses; no human data.
note: Preclinical only; banned in sport; unapproved.
currentQuick:
LGD-3303 is an experimental SARM made by Ligand Pharmaceuticals. Animal studies looked at its effects on muscle, bone and female sexual behaviour.
No human trial has been registered, so its effects in people are unknown.
How it works: It activates the androgen receptor; in rats it stimulated muscle strongly while only partially stimulating prostate tissue.
Risks and caveats: There are no human safety data. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned in sport, and linked in reports to liver injury.
deepLead:
LGD-3303 is an investigational, orally available nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals, with a tricyclic pyrrolo[3,2-f]quinolin-7-one structure . Published work consists of animal and in vitro studies of its pharmacokinetics, muscle and bone effects and effects on sexual behaviour in female rats .
No registered human trial was found, and it is not approved for any use . SARMs are prohibited in sport, and detection studies of LGD-3303 metabolites in horses have been published .
